newsitem.title: UK: Stanley Leisure cuts gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Stanley Leisure cuts gains on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in leisure services group Stanley Leisure Plc slipped from an earlier record high on Monday as analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson advised taking profits on the stock.
The shares were up 1/2p at 306-1/2p by 1158 GMT after slipping from an all-time high of 310p.
Earlier the company announced the acquisition of 30 betting shops for 8.0 million stg.

"Given the significant outperformance and the heady rating that the shares attract, we believe that now is an appropriate time to take profits," said Greg Feehely, analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson. The shares have risen 23 percent since the start of this year.

Additionally, in his latest research note Feehely said he had downgraded his current year profit forecast for the group to 19.6 million stg from 20.9 million stg, following the group's interim results.
The analyst said margin pressure and the relatively small three percent increase in core betting turnover was of concern.
"Further casino deregulation, when it comes could add 4.0-5.0 million pounds to Stanley's bottom line but would leave the stock on a significant premium to the market (25-30 percent)," Feehely said.
